definition: The time or occasion of the full moon; also, the full moon itself.
etymology: From Latin plenus, meaning full, joined to luna, the moon. Roman poets leaned on plenus whenever they wanted to press maximum weight into a single syllable, and plenilune carries that same sense of something filled to its absolute brim. It entered English through medieval astronomical Latin in the fourteenth century, riding the same learned tide that brought us solstice and equinox.
usage: June's full moon falls just after the solstice this year, making plenilune an apt word for the week: the sky offers its longest night lit not by darkness but by that swollen, brimming disc, and plenilune says exactly that without requiring a single extra word.
